headline: Modest sales growth, softer margins and transition costs
summary_short: Pool Corp's Q2 2026 net sales rose 2% y/y to $1.82B, but GAAP net income fell 3% to $188.1M as higher freight costs, an unfavorable customer mix and $8.3M of CEO transition costs weighed on margins. Adjusted net income rose 1% to $195.7M.
summary_long: Net sales grew 2% y/y to $1.82B on ~3% inflationary pricing, steady maintenance demand and 4% building-materials growth, partly offset by weak discretionary spending. Gross margin fell 30bp to 29.7% on higher freight and unfavorable customer mix, partly offset by supply-chain initiatives. Opex rose 4% on $8.3M of one-time CEO transition costs; adjusted opex rose 1%. Operating income fell 2% to $267.7M (adjusted +1% to $275.9M); net income fell 3% to $188.1M despite a higher 25.8% tax rate. The board raised buyback authorization to $600M ($580M remaining) and declared a $1.30/share dividend, up 4% y/y. FY2026 guidance: gross margin ~30bp below 2025's 29.7%, opex +2-3% ex CEO costs, diluted EPS $10.66-$10.96.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: growth was driven by a ~3% benefit from inflationary product cost increases, steady maintenance demand and building-materials sales (+4%), partly offset by weaker discretionary spending.
Company-disclosed: sales growth outpaced a 30bp gross-margin decline caused by elevated inbound freight costs and an unfavorable customer mix, partly offset by supply-chain initiatives.
Company-disclosed: $8.3M of one-time CEO transition costs pushed operating expenses up 4%, outweighing the gross-profit gain; adjusted operating income (ex-transition costs) rose 1%.
Derived-arithmetic: EBITDA fell 1.2% y/y, tracking the operating-income decline since depreciation and amortization added back were little changed y/y.
Company-disclosed: decline reflects the CEO transition costs and a higher effective tax rate (25.8% vs 25.4% a year ago), partly offset by revenue growth; adjusted net income rose 1%.
Derived-arithmetic: diluted EPS held at $5.17 as the net-income decline was offset by a lower diluted share count (36.1M vs 37.4M) from ongoing buybacks; adjusted diluted EPS rose 4% to $5.38.
Derived-arithmetic: basic EPS was essentially flat at $5.18 vs $5.19, tracking the same net-income and share-count dynamics as diluted EPS.
Company-disclosed: the board declared $1.30 per share for the quarter, up from $1.25 a year earlier.

Company-disclosed: management called Q2 weather impact broadly neutral and outlined FY2026 expectations (freight-cost pressure, supply-chain benefits, opportunistic buybacks) without stating a formal raise or cut to prior guidance.
